correctness.rationale: The vertex-edge exchange characterization is a standard matroid-base-polytope theorem. For each matched-pair node, swapping its own U and D is admissible exactly below depth one. For any distinct node pair, the possible two swaps contribute 0 for a root and its descendant, 2 for nodes sharing one depth-two child subtree, 1 otherwise. The \(n-r\) exclusions and \(n-r\) self-node additions cancel, proving the degree identity. Root-component combinatorial decomposition gives the formal GF and recurrence; convexity of binomial(s,2) over disjoint child blocks gives min/max plus sharp equality. Independent direct enumeration \(1\le n\le9\) confirms all per-word degrees and exact polynomial coefficients and equality counts. Finite enumeration is not used to prove the infinite statement.

value.rationale: This gives the entire vertex-degree polynomial for the one-skeleton of a Catalan matroid polytope, a Catalan-size family whose exchange dynamics were studied but whose published aggregates did not describe the local degree distribution. The depth-two block collapse gives structural information on bottlenecks and extremal exchange mobility; the multiplicities \(2^{n-1}\) and \(C_{n-2}\) distinguish exponentially many least-mobile vertices from the sharply constrained maximizers. Exact complete graph-degree distributions are natural invariant refinements beyond aggregate f-vectors, not arbitrary parameter slices.
